prompt: Find a word in a printed dictionary by opening to the middle and halving the pages each time.
why: Each look cuts the remaining pages in half, so even a huge dictionary takes few steps. Halving the search each time is O(log n).

prompt: Guess a number from 1 to 1,000 with higher-or-lower hints in about 10 tries.
why: Each higher-or-lower hint halves the range: 1,000 to 500 to 250 and so on, about 10 steps. Repeated halving is O(log n).
trap: Ten tries for a thousand isn't linear.

prompt: Doubling the data adds only one more step to the search.
why: Doubling the data only adds one more halving step to the search. Growth that slow is logarithmic, O(log n).
trap: Constant time would add no steps at all.

prompt: Binary search through a sorted list of a million names takes about 20 checks.
why: A million halves to one in about 20 steps, since 2 to the 20th is about a million. Binary search is O(log n).
trap: It's small but it does grow.

prompt: Each step of a balanced tree lookup throws away half of what's left.
tells: throws away half of what's left
why: Each step down a balanced tree discards half of what's left, so a lookup takes about log n steps. That's O(log n).

prompt: Adding to a heap of a million items takes around 20 swaps up the tree.
why: A new item swaps up one level at a time, and a heap of a million is only about 20 levels tall. Tree height is log n, so insert is O(log n).
trap: It isn't one step, and it isn't a million.
